title: Commander U Riddle for 8.5 BTC

prize.note: 8.5 BTC of this sits in a 2010 P2PK output, which mempool.space's address API does not index; it shows only the 99,081 sats held in 8 separate P2PKH outputs at the same address. Both readings are correct for what each indexer counts; the full total is spendable by the one private key that controls both, since the P2PKH outputs derive from the same uncompressed public key exposed by the P2PK output

addresses.label: the announced prize address
addresses.expected: 8.50099081 BTC (850,000,000 sats P2PK, not shown by mempool.space; 99,081 sats P2PKH, shown)

target_format: 51-character uncompressed mainnet WIF (6 concatenated base58 fragments, lengths 9, 8, 9, 9, 8, 8), matching P2PKH address 1KDUcZh5Z6H1of4Pwoy5ojJtkQxcQBHhnH and uncompressed public key 041ebfac69910efb17ab697db5f2a4ff815e1d37c05e40d56977031a3a36b80464ea6782ad2913e2a5ec33e187f0fee50675bc78a25d657846e08e8425f2384b2a

derivation.summary: concatenate 6 base58 fragments, each meant to be recovered by solving one sub-riddle and checked against a per-fragment MD5 hash, into a 51-character WIF; decode it to a private key; the resulting uncompressed public key must equal the known exposed public key exactly

difficulty_note: 4 of 6 fragments are unrecovered; one has no published checksum at all, and 3 do not match the MD5 of any base58 string of the stated length under any of 28 standard transforms tried; the missing piece is the original 2019 channel with the sub-riddle answers, which I could not find, and which may never have existed as a real puzzle in the first place
third_party_material: the site's own hint text and fragment table, reproduced as published; no third-party copyrighted material
